OAuth sign-in works again: the redirect URL had a trailing slash, so GitHub rejected it, and now it matches the one in the app settings.
We compared four small models on 192 lines, and the clearest one misread about five words in a hundred, close to what the teacher model does.

Here's where things stand. The fix for the download bar is live, and nano now shows its real size of about eleven megabytes. The bench page runs each model on its own, so your phone never holds two copies. I'll send the numbers as soon as your run lands.

A volcano is a place where very hot, melted rock comes up out of the ground. Ash and smoky gases can come out too. Deep under the ground, the melted rock waits in a big pool called a magma chamber. When the pressure gets too high, it pushes up and erupts.

I went through the failing tests. Two of them were flaky and depended on the clock, so I made them use a fake timer. The third one was real: the parser dropped the last line of a file without a newline at the end. That's fixed, and all 412 tests pass now.

Your week looks busy. On Monday you have the board update at 10:00. Tuesday is free until the dentist at 4:30 PM. Wednesday has two calls with the release team, and on Friday the launch goes out at 9:00 AM Pacific time.

We tried three ways to make the phone faster. Using all four CPU cores helped the most, about forty percent. Turning off the graph optimizer saved memory but cost a little speed. WebGPU was fastest on the Mac, but it crashed the tab on iOS, so we left it off there.

The new pricing page is ready for review. The basic plan stays at $9 a month, the team plan goes from $29 to $24 per seat, and annual billing saves two months. I kept the free tier, but it now has a limit of three projects instead of five.

Last night the agents ran 146 jobs. 139 finished, four were retried and passed, and three failed because the GPU quota ran out at 3:20 AM. I moved those three to this morning's queue, and they should be done before your first meeting.

To set it up, clone the repository, run npm install, and copy .env.example to .env.local. Then start the dev server with npm run dev and open localhost on port 5780. The first load downloads the voice, which takes about ten seconds on Wi-Fi.

The model card needs three things before we publish: the speed table from real devices, the clarity scores per voice, and a short note on what the model is not good at. I have the first two drafts ready, and the speed runs are going now.

Here is the short version of the incident. At 14:02 the database ran out of connections, the API started returning errors, and about 8% of requests failed for six minutes. We raised the pool size, added an alert at 80% use, and wrote up the timeline for the team.
